title: Primary economic activities
competency: Explain agriculture, forestry, fishing and mining.

keywords.def: Taking resources directly from the environment: agriculture, forestry, fishing, mining.
The science and art of cultivating the soil and rearing livestock.
Obtaining useful minerals such as coal, gold or iron ore from the earth's crust.

en.text: Primary activities take resources directly from the environment: agriculture (crops and livestock), forestry (timber, fuel wood, carbon sinks), fishing and mining (coal, gold, iron ore). Agriculture is the basic livelihood of most Ethiopians.

am.text: የመጀመሪያ ደረጃ እንቅስቃሴዎች ሀብትን በቀጥታ ከተፈጥሮ ይወስዳሉ፤ ግብርና፣ ደን፣ ዓሣ ማጥመድና ማዕድን ማውጣት።

screens.title: Wheat farm
screens.ask: A farmer in Arsi grows wheat. Is she making something from raw materials, or taking food from the land?
opts: Taking from the land: a primary activity
screens.after: Farming takes resources directly from the environment. That is a primary activity.

screens.title: Primary economic activities
paras: Primary activities take resources directly from the environment.
They produce foodstuffs and raw materials.
table: Taking forest products from plantations and natural forests
Catching fish and other water creatures
Getting minerals like coal, gold and iron ore from the crust

screens.title: Why they matter
paras: Agriculture gives food and raw materials for industries. It is the basic livelihood of most Ethiopians.
Forests give timber, fuel wood, wildlife habitat and act as "sinks" for carbon dioxide.
Ethiopia has many fish-rich lakes and rivers, but fishing is not well developed.

screens.text: Which is a primary economic activity?
Agriculture involves crop production and livestock rearing.

screens.text: Gold from Shakiso is dug out, then made into jewellery in Addis Ababa. Which step is primary?
screens.why: Mining (getting minerals from the crust) is primary. Making jewellery is secondary; selling is tertiary.
